comment: Super easy class, midterm was hard for a lot of people, but as long as you truly study the study guide it really is not that bad. Easy to participate. Philosophical guy that kind of sees everything as a possibility, but overall enjoyed his class and was an easy A. No final either!

Disliked the overall class and its structure, but pretty easy to get an A, just incredibly boring- to be fair, I did not have any prior interest in PLSC, but students who did have prior interest appeared to enjoy the class. The professor is very into mediation, which leads to slow, frustrating class starts.

dr. datta can sometimes seem like he has bigger priorities than teaching, and sometimes forgets to introduce assignments until right before they are due/warn about a quiz the day before. however, he clearly is passionate about his field and makes sure everyone feels welcome and has a chance to speak.
he is a good teacher.

Extremely caring professor, especially when it comes to mental health. Lots of guest speakers and loves to do group work/simulations. Super chill guy who is very knowledgable which makes class enjoyable. Pretty easy class: a few quizzes on the readings, reflection papers, and one final paper worth 40% of your grade. No midterm or final exam
Phenomenal! If you need to take this class take it with Datta. Very fair grader, and if you put in the work no reason you can't do well.

I took Global Governance with Datta last semester, and I plan on taking him as much as possible once he comes back from his sabbatical. He is, without a doubt, the best professor in the Political Science department at UR. He values student mental health highly and cares about one's personal development rather than specific assignments and grades.

Dr. Datta is a knowledgeable, caring, and relatable professor who genuinely invests in his students. There are textbook readings assigned each week, but he goes over the important concepts in the weekly lecture so... 
your grade is basically two papers and two exams, but he grades very generously. Would Recommend.

Dr. Datta is a very kind person and fantastic professor. He is a very intelligent man who knows a lot about what he is teaching, which is very evident in lectures and class discussions. This class was a lot of fun and not too work heavy. I would recommend this class to anyone considering taking an introductory political science class.

Dr. Datta is AMAZING! It's incredibly obvious that he cares a lot about his students and is very passionate about the subjects he teaches. He makes lectures and discussions fun, but also is really helpful with feedback and furthering understanding of the course
Dr. Datta is one of the kindest professors at Richmond. Not much work and grades super easily. Cares so much for his students and is an insanely smart guy. Def recommend
Dr. Datta is a great guy and a solid teacher too. If you want to take an intro class in poli sci, take one of his classes. He is a little kookie but a clear and easy grader.
An awesome professor! He treats his students with so much respect. He helps you by going above and beyond!! Grades very easy

Dr. Datta quickly became one of my favorite professors at UR. He cares very deeply for his studentsfrequently moving deadlines and editing lectures based on class feedback. He is a great example of how professors should respect their students, and a wonderful lecturer as well. The content was easily understood, and the tests applied it well.
Super nice and caring. Pretty easy. The whole grade is pretty much based on exams and 2 papers.

Monti Datta is one of the best professors at Richmond. He genuinely cares about all his students and has been one of the most supportive professors in my academic career. He practices mindfulness and is insanely smart. A must take professor.

Dr. Datta is a great guy and believes that his students can be great, too. He made sure to listen to our opinions on different assignments or debates in class, and I really appreciated that. The class, however, was really unstructured, and it became irritating as the semester progressed. Otherwise, the class was both interesting and easy.
easy class, nice guy but we didn't follow the syllabus and I don't feel like i learned anything

Dr. Datta is a great professor. He always comes prepared and he truly cares about his students. He may even extend deadlines for the entire class if you are too stressed. The class is very interactive with cool simulations. There's lots of reading and 3 papers, but the class is still chill and you can always skim the reading and still participate.

Dr. Datta is easily the most caring professor I've had here at UR. The extreme compassion and desire for his students to learn and excel is unparalleled. His class generates incredible discussion, and he grades very fairly while clearly outlining his expectations. One of the best professors you'll have here for sure

Dr. Datta was a wonderful professor that went out of his way to help you in any way that he could. As of now he is conducting research in Thailand and won't be back til fall of 2017. If you need to fulfill your social science inquiry requirement I would highly recommend waiting until he gets back. He is the only way to go for this class. Great guy.
Dr. Datta is a really nice guy who loves international relations. The class is not particularly challenging, which at times means it can be boring. I would probably take it again.

I've never met such a nice person, let alone teacher. He will actually ask you if there is something in class you want to talk about more and then he does. Who does that? He assigned 2 papers and 2 online tests throughout the year and the lectures tend to get a bit dry but he incorporates current events very well into them.

Dr. Datta's course on Human Trafficking was incredible! It was one of the most valuable courses I have taken so far. The guest speakers he brought in to the course were interesting and he made the class engaging.

Professor Datta gives 2 papers, a midterm and a final. The papers are both 10 pages long and he gives multiple options for you to choose your topic. Midterm is very easy, all definitions of concepts, and final was online. Barely any work outside of class besides papers. Really nice guy and good teacher in general.

Datta is a nice guy and means really well despite being a little odd.  Hard not to get an A or a B although sometimes the class can get painfully boring.  A good intro level class and I would suggest taking him for sure.
Best professor I've had at UR. So smart and still SUCH a good teacher. His classes are really interesting and he incorporates current events into them.

Seems like a nice guy, somewhat awkward though. Very responsive to student feedback. Graded the papers super easy. Was very enthusiastic about subject. Wanted students to do well and tried to show he cared.

Dr. Datta is a very enthusiastic teacher who genuinely wants students to learn and be challenged.  This was however a very easy, straightforward class with minimal work.  I felt as though I may not have been as prepared as possible for higher level courses in the field.
Dr. Datta is fantastic. He truly cares about the well-being and success of his students. He?s well prepared and enthusiastic during lectures. I really enjoyed going to class.

Dr. Datta isn't bad. There was a lot of reading and quizzes on the reading. Sometimes he was cryptic with questions about the quizzes. He's also very helpful and will meet with you at anytime to help you on the term paper. He's new and a little nervous but I think that the more he teaches the better he'll be.

Wonderful professor, he teaches well and genuinely cares about his students. He wants you to do well and it a great teacher. There is reading and a few papers but compared to other classes, he makes this one a breeze. I highly recommend taking one of his classes.

Dr. Datta is very nice but kind of goofy and eccentric. The class itself is heavily theory based but not too complicated. Quizzes are easy and there is only a 48 hour midterm essay and 10 page term paper that were the big grades for the class. Not a bad class to take, he teaches it in a way to make some of the more dry concepts interesting.
